rationale: The blind translation is a faithful explicit rendering of Exercise 2.7.2 and Proposition 2.7.1(a)--(d): one universal absolute factor converts any of the four formulations at any positive input scale into any other at a positive scale within that factor. It preserves the tail rate, moment growth, absolute-value exponential moments, all parameter domains and endpoints, the coefficient 2, the absence of centering, and the distinction between C, Ki, and Kj. Its explicit measurability and integrability clauses express conventions already implicit in the source, and its raw-moment presentation is equivalent to the source's L^p-norm presentation. Both implications therefore hold, no checklist item is unresolved, and adjudication is unnecessary.
